name: Telford
note: New town renamed Telford in 1968 after the civil engineer Thomas Telford; not a ford name

name: Gifford
note: Named from the 13th-century Sir Hugo de Giffard of Yester; not a ford name

name: Milford Haven
note: Milford is from Old Norse Melfjordr, 'fjord of the sandbank'; not a ford

name: Seaforth
note: Recorded as Safforde 'sea ford' in 1128, but also explained as Old Norse 'sea inlet' or as taken from Seaforth House; kept as ford but flagged

name: Bridgwater
note: Origin disputed: possibly Old English brycg or Old Norse bryggja 'quay', with Walter of Douai; also read as 'Walter's bridge'; added as bridge but flagged

name: Bridgnorth
note: Crossing word first (bridge over the Severn); I could not re-read a source for the detail in this study, so it is flagged

name: Brigg
note: Old Norse bryggja 'jetty, quay', here referring to the bridge over the River Ancholme (the town was Glanford Brigg)

name: Brighouse
note: 'Bridge house': a building on or close to the bridge over the River Calder

name: Cambridge
note: Old English Grantebrycge: the name came to mean 'the bridge over the Granta'; kept as a bridge

name: Pontcanna
note: From Pont Canna Farm, named after a bridge across the Whitehouse Brook

name: Bridport
note: From Brydian 'place at the (River) Bride' plus port 'market town'; not a bridge (the rules do not catch it)

name: Bridlington
note: A personal name plus -ingtun; recorded as Bretlinton in 1086; not a bridge (the rules do not catch it)
